paper.title: Do People Respond to the Mortgage Interest Deduction? Quasi-Experimental Evidence from Denmark
paper.code_data_availability: Replication data are cited as: Gruber, Jonathan, Amalie Jensen, and Henrik Kleven. …

outcomes (homeownership from whether the home is occupied by the owner; home size) and linkage via home address code / property identification number
outcomes (home value, from the Danish Tax Authorities' appraisal)
linkage (families: spouses/cohabitants and children, used for the household-based homeownership and tax-treatment measures)

treatment (income and tax-bracket position, used to assign top/middle/bottom bracket from 1984-1986) and outcomes (deductible interest expenses); individual tax files on owned property from 1987 onward

registers.name_in_paper: Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Residential Property Price Database, 1983-1996
registers.role: outcomes for the cross-country synthetic control analysis (quarterly real residential property prices for Denmark and 16 donor countries)

registers.name_in_paper: Danish Ministry of Taxation, Tax Rates over Time, 1980-2017
registers.role: treatment (statutory marginal tax rates on negative and positive net capital income by bracket, Figure 1)
variables_mentioned: marginal tax rate on negative net capital income
marginal tax rate on positive net capital income

linkages: Administrative registers linked at the individual level through personal identification numbers.
Each individual has a home address code and a property identification number, which link to a housing register with information on homeownership and property characteristics.
Individuals linked to their spouses/cohabitants and children, which is used to build household-based measures of homeownership and of tax treatment.
Individuals in multi-person owner-occupied homes linked to the individual tax files on owned property available from 1987 onward, to assign owner status in earlier years.

sample.universe: Administrative data for the full Danish population from 1980 to 2011.
sample.unit_of_observation: individual-year (the analysis is implemented on individuals but is in reality household-based: both homeownership and tax treatment are defined at the household level)
selection_rules: Drop all children living with their parents.

Define everyone living in a home not occupied by the owner as a renter; assign owner status in owner-occupied homes (single occupant = owner; married/cohabiting couple = both owners; multi-person households assigned using the individual tax files on owned property from 1987).
Drop the small group of individuals for whom owner/renter status cannot be assigned.
Keep individuals observed in every year of the analysis window (a semibalanced panel; 1980-1996 for the main analyses, 1980-2011 for the long-run analyses, 1983-1996 for interest expenses).
Restrict to ages 20-80: individuals drop out after turning 80 and enter only after turning 20.

Assign treatment status from household tax-bracket position in every one of the three pre-reform years 1984-1986; drop taxpayers who move across brackets during 1984-1986 (about 13 percent of the sample).
For the home size and home value analyses, select the repeated cross-section of households who move in the given year.
For the interest-expenses analysis, start in 1983 rather than 1980 because nominal interest rates fell sharply between 1982 and 1983.
sample.period: 1980-2011 (main analyses on a semibalanced panel observed every year 1980-1996; long-run panel 1980-2011; interest expenses 1983-1996; cross-country house prices 1983:I-1996:IV)
sample.n_observations: about 40 million individual-year observations in the semibalanced 1980-1996 panel; 34,440,869 observations in the top-versus-below-top homeownership regression

construction_notes: Homeownership is defined at the household level because individuals and homes are matched via the home address; an individual is a homeowner if she and/or her spouse are registered as homeowners.
The homeownership measure is validated in online Appendix Figure A.I against the ideal tax-based measure available from 1987.

Home size is the area of the house used for habitation; it is trimmed at the fifth and ninety-fifth percentile. Section IIB describes it in square meters, while the title and notes of Figure 4 and Table 2 call it square feet.
Home value is a desk appraisal by the Danish Tax Authorities, known to be noisy, not updated every year for every house, and set below market value.
Interest expenses are total deductible interest (mortgage, consumer and other debt); mortgage interest cannot be observed separately over the whole period. They are third-party reported by lenders.
Tax treatment is household-based: a taxpayer is in the top bracket if she or her spouse is; in the middle bracket if she or her spouse is and neither is in the top; in the bottom bracket if both are.

All table estimates residualize the outcome on a group-specific linear time trend estimated with age dummies on the four last pre-reform years 1983-1986, and then run specification (11)/(12) on the full period using the residualized outcome.
Cross-country house prices are real: nominal BIS residential property prices deflated by the Consumer Price Index, each series normalized to 100 in 1986:IV.
Standard errors are clustered at the household level throughout the micro analysis.

links.pointer_quote: Over multiple time periods, and considering multiple empirical strategies, we find no effect of the tax policy change on whether these households own or rent.

claims.statement: The 1987 Danish tax reform's scaling back of the mortgage interest deduction had no economically relevant effect on Homeowner rate among Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 assigned to the top tax bracket in every year 1984-1986 (column 1: no age controls).

treatment.label: Effect of reform (post × treat: exposure to the 1987 scaling back of the mortgage interest deduction)

register_source.value: IND (Indkomst, Income) individual income tax records, tax-bracket position 1984-1986

definition.value: The interaction post_t · treat_i in equation (12). treat_i = 1 for taxpayers assigned to the top tax bracket in every one of the three pre-reform years 1984-1986 (a taxpayer is assigned to the top bracket if either she or her spouse is in the top bracket); post_t = 1 from 1987 onwards. The control group is taxpayers below the top bracket (middle and bottom brackets combined) in every year 1984-1986. The 1987 reform raised the net-of-tax interest rate on negative capital income by 81 percent for the top group, 29 percent for the middle group and −6 percent for the bottom group.

timing.value: Treatment status assigned from pre-reform tax-bracket status in every year 1984-1986; treatment switched on in 1987, the year of the reform.

register_source.value: BOL (Boligtaellingen, Homes) housing register linked to individuals via the home address code and property identification number; individual tax files on owned property from 1987 used for the multi-person-household cases

definition.value: Indicator for whether the individual is a homeowner, measured at the household level: an individual is a homeowner if she and/or her spouse/cohabitant are registered as living in an owner-occupied home in the housing register (children living with parents dropped; people whose owner/renter status cannot be assigned dropped). The outcome entering equation (12) is residualized on a group-specific linear pre-trend estimated on 1983-1986.

timing.value: Measured annually; the coefficient is the average effect over the ten post-reform years (1987-1996) relative to the pre-reform years.

units.value: change in the homeowner rate, in proportion units (0.001 = 0.1 percentage points)

magnitude.interpretation: the effect of the reform on homeownership is very small across all specifications

estimand.target_population: High-income (top-bracket) Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 treated by the 1987 reform, relative to taxpayers below the top bracket (middle and bottom brackets combined) in every year 1984-1986
estimand.time_horizon: average effect over the ten post-reform years 1987-1996

population.description: Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 assigned to the top tax bracket in every year 1984-1986 (treatments) versus taxpayers below the top bracket in every year 1984-1986 (controls)
population.selection: Sample selection: individuals must be observed in every year of the panel (1980-1996), be aged 20-80, and be in the same tax bracket in all three pre-reform years 1984-1986 (bracket switchers, about 13 percent of the sample, are dropped); individuals whose owner/renter status cannot be assigned are dropped.

identification.source_of_variation: The 1987 Danish tax reform, which introduced dual income taxation and taxed negative capital income at the bottom rate. It raised the net-of-tax interest rate on negative capital income by 81 percent for the top bracket, 29 percent for the middle bracket, and lowered it by 6 percent for the bottom bracket.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the 1987 reform, the outcome of the top-bracket group and of taxpayers below the top bracket (middle and bottom brackets combined) in every year 1984-1986 would have evolved in parallel (after absorbing life-cycle/age effects and a group-specific linear pre-trend).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Observed pre-reform trends in Figures 3-6; all table estimates are additionally adjusted for group-specific linear pre-trends estimated on 1983-1986.

formal.statement: E[Y(0)_top,post − Y(0)_top,pre] = E[Y(0)_control,post − Y(0)_control,pre]

key_assumptions.assumption: Homogeneous responsiveness: the below-top control group is itself partly treated (the middle bracket saw a 29 percent rise in the net-of-tax rate), so the difference-in-differences recovers the elasticity only if treatments and controls respond homogeneously to the tax price.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the trade-off explicitly and reports the top-versus-bottom comparison (panel B), which does not require it.

formal.statement: The tax-price elasticity is constant across the top and below-top groups.

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference between treatment and control groups: the estimate is a partial-equilibrium (micro) elasticity that takes the rental rate r and the mortgage interest rate m as given, so the reform's general-equilibrium effect on prices is assumed not to shift the control group's outcome.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper flags the micro-versus-macro distinction, and Section V separately estimates a national house-price effect.

implies_edges.from: equilibrium house and rental prices

formal.statement: No edge from the treated group's reform exposure to the control group's outcome (no spillover through equilibrium house and rental prices).

key_assumptions.assumption: Sample selection: individuals must be observed in every year of the panel (1980-1996), be aged 20-80, and be in the same tax bracket in all three pre-reform years 1984-1986 (bracket switchers, about 13 percent of the sample, are dropped); individuals whose owner/renter status cannot be assigned are dropped. These conditioning events are assumed not to be differentially affected by the reform.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the panel and bracket-stability restrictions and the share of the sample they drop.

implies_edges.from: panel survival 1980-1996, age 20-80 and stable tax bracket 1984-1986

formal.statement: The analysis conditions on panel survival, bracket stability 1984-1986.

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: outcomes in the pre-reform years 1984-1986, which are used to assign treatment status and to estimate the group-specific linear pre-trend, are not already responding to the 1987 reform.

implies_edges.from: Effect of reform (post × treat: exposure to the 1987 scaling back of the mortgage interest deduction)

formal.statement: No edge from the (future) 1987 reform to pre-1987 outcomes.

key_assumptions.assumption: Age effects are modelled as stated by column 1: no age controls: the DiD is only free of differential life-cycle composition if the age specification used in this column absorbs it.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper shows graphically that nonparametric, group-specific age dummies absorb differential life-cycle trends, and reports columns 1-3 to show how the estimate moves with the age specification.

formal.statement: Age enters additively through no age term.

estimator.value: OLS difference-in-differences on a pre-trend-residualized outcome (equation 12)

estimation.specification: Equation (12); column 1: no age controls
controls: group-specific linear pre-trend (outcome residualized, estimated on 1983-1986)

heterogeneity.dimension: control group (below-top bracket versus bottom bracket)
heterogeneity.finding: Panel A compares the top bracket to everyone below it; panel B compares the top bracket to the bottom bracket only. The reform effect is larger in absolute value in panel B for home size and home value, which the paper attributes to the larger underlying tax variation; the elasticities vary much less across the two comparisons.
Columns 1-3 move from no age controls to common age dummies to group-specific age dummies; the paper's preferred estimate is column 3.

ambiguities: The paper prints no significance stars, p-values or confidence intervals in any table; statistically_significant was set from the printed estimate/standard-error ratio.

relationship.sign records the printed sign of this coefficient (transcription). The paper's own reading of Table 1 is that these are economic zeros, which is why the graph edge is causal_tested_null rather than causal_tested: the estimates are many standard errors from zero but less than one percentage point in size.

evidence.panel: Panel A. Top versus below-top groups

evidence.how: statistically_significant set from the printed estimate and its printed standard error (|estimate| / SE >= 2.5 -> true; otherwise left null). The paper itself prints no significance markers or p-values.
The outcome is a 0/1 homeowner indicator and the text reads the panel B column 3 estimate of −0.002 as "less than one-quarter of a percentage point", so the coefficients are in proportion units.

evidence.annotation: The actual homeowner rates in 1986 were 83.7 percent for taxpayers in the top bracket and 62.0 percent for taxpayers below the top bracket.

value.as_printed: Y^R_it = α_0 + α_1 · post_t + α_2 · treat_i + α_3 · post_t · treat_i + Σ_a β_a · 1(a = age_it) + Σ_a β^T_a · 1(a = age_it) · treat_i + ν_it
value.lhs: Y^R_it (Homeowner rate, residualized on a group-specific linear pre-trend)
value.normalisation: Column 1 drops both age-dummy terms of equation (12); the outcome is residualized on a group-specific linear pre-trend estimated on 1983-1986, and 1986 is the last pre-reform year.

value.claimed_domain: High- and middle-income Danish households, roughly the upper half of the income distribution, who are the households treated by the 1987 reform. The paper states explicitly that its homeownership results apply to both top-rate and middle-rate taxpayers.
boundary_conditions: Only high- and middle-income households are treated by the reform; the effects may be different at the bottom of the income distribution.
The reform does not allow responses in the lower half of the income distribution to be identified.
A Danish setting in which imputed rental income was taxed, albeit at an artificially low level.

theory_referenced: A simple housing market model with intensive- and extensive-margin demand responses to taxes (Section III, equations 1-10), which defines the intensive-margin elasticity ε and the extensive-margin elasticity η.
outcomes_examined_not_reported: Propensity to move (analysed; the paper reports no clear effect but prints no estimate).
Home size when always-renters are dropped (the paper says it obtains very similar results but does not report them).

claims.statement: The 1987 Danish tax reform's scaling back of the mortgage interest deduction had no economically relevant effect on Homeowner rate among Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 assigned to the top tax bracket in every year 1984-1986 (column 1: no age controls).

treatment.label: Effect of reform (post × treat: exposure to the 1987 scaling back of the mortgage interest deduction)

register_source.value: IND (Indkomst, Income) individual income tax records, tax-bracket position 1984-1986

definition.value: The interaction post_t · treat_i in equation (12). treat_i = 1 for taxpayers assigned to the top tax bracket in every one of the three pre-reform years 1984-1986 (a taxpayer is assigned to the top bracket if either she or her spouse is in the top bracket); post_t = 1 from 1987 onwards. register_source.value: Danish Ministry of Taxation, statutory marginal tax rates on capital income (Figure 1)

definition.value: The elasticity is ε = α̂_3 / [Δlog(1 − τ^T) − Δlog(1 − τ^C)] (equation 13), where Δlog(1 − τ^g) is the reform-induced change in the net-of-tax rate on negative capital income for group g between 1986 and 1987. The reform raised this rate by 81 percent for the top group, 29 percent for the middle group and −6 percent for the bottom group.

timing.value: Change in the statutory net-of-tax rate between 1986 and 1987.

register_source.value: BOL (Boligtaellingen, Homes) housing register property characteristics

definition.value: Natural log of home size, where home size is the area of the house used for habitation, trimmed at the fifth and ninety-fifth percentile. The outcome entering equation (12) is residualized on a group-specific linear pre-trend estimated on 1983-1986.

timing.value: Measured annually; the coefficient is the average effect over the ten post-reform years (1987-1996) relative to the pre-reform years.

units.value: elasticity of home size with respect to the net-of-tax rate 1 − τ (unitless)

magnitude.interpretation: the elasticity of home size lies between 0.09 and 0.12

estimand.target_population: High-income (top-bracket) Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 treated by the 1987 reform, relative to taxpayers below the top bracket (middle and bottom brackets combined) in every year 1984-1986
estimand.time_horizon: average effect over the ten post-reform years 1987-1996

population.description: Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 assigned to the top tax bracket in every year 1984-1986 (treatments) versus taxpayers below the top bracket in every year 1984-1986 (controls)
population.selection: Sample selection: individuals must be observed in every year of the panel (1980-1996), be aged 20-80, and be in the same tax bracket in all three pre-reform years 1984-1986 (bracket switchers, about 13 percent of the sample, are dropped); individuals whose owner/renter status cannot be assigned are dropped. In addition, the estimation sample is the repeated cross-section of households who move in the given year.

identification.source_of_variation: The 1987 Danish tax reform, which introduced dual income taxation and taxed negative capital income at the bottom rate. It raised the net-of-tax interest rate on negative capital income by 81 percent for the top bracket, 29 percent for the middle bracket, and lowered it by 6 percent for the bottom bracket.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the 1987 reform, the outcome of the top-bracket group and of taxpayers below the top bracket (middle and bottom brackets combined) in every year 1984-1986 would have evolved in parallel (after absorbing life-cycle/age effects and a group-specific linear pre-trend).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Observed pre-reform trends in Figures 3-6; all table estimates are additionally adjusted for group-specific linear pre-trends estimated on 1983-1986.

formal.statement: E[Y(0)_top,post − Y(0)_top,pre] = E[Y(0)_control,post − Y(0)_control,pre]

key_assumptions.assumption: Homogeneous responsiveness: the below-top control group is itself partly treated (the middle bracket saw a 29 percent rise in the net-of-tax rate), so the difference-in-differences recovers the elasticity only if treatments and controls respond homogeneously to the tax price.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the trade-off explicitly and reports the top-versus-bottom comparison (panel B), which does not require it.

formal.statement: The tax-price elasticity is constant across the top and below-top groups.

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference between treatment and control groups: the estimate is a partial-equilibrium (micro) elasticity that takes the rental rate r and the mortgage interest rate m as given, so the reform's general-equilibrium effect on prices is assumed not to shift the control group's outcome.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper flags the micro-versus-macro distinction, and Section V separately estimates a national house-price effect.

implies_edges.from: equilibrium house and rental prices

formal.statement: No edge from the treated group's reform exposure to the control group's outcome (no spillover through equilibrium house and rental prices).

key_assumptions.assumption: Sample selection: individuals must be observed in every year of the panel (1980-1996), be aged 20-80, and be in the same tax bracket in all three pre-reform years 1984-1986 (bracket switchers, about 13 percent of the sample, are dropped); individuals whose owner/renter status cannot be assigned are dropped. In addition, the estimation sample is the repeated cross-section of households who move in the given year. These conditioning events are assumed not to be differentially affected by the reform.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper reports that it analysed the moving margin and found no clear effect of the reform on the propensity to move.

moving in the given year

formal.statement: The analysis conditions on panel survival, bracket stability 1984-1986, and on moving in the given year.

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: outcomes in the pre-reform years 1984-1986, which are used to assign treatment status and to estimate the group-specific linear pre-trend, are not already responding to the 1987 reform.

implies_edges.from: Net-of-tax rate 1 − τ on negative capital income

formal.statement: No edge from the (future) 1987 reform to pre-1987 outcomes.

key_assumptions.assumption: Age effects are modelled as stated by column 2: common age fixed effects: the DiD is only free of differential life-cycle composition if the age specification used in this column absorbs it.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper shows graphically that nonparametric, group-specific age dummies absorb differential life-cycle trends, and reports columns 1-3 to show how the estimate moves with the age specification.

formal.statement: Age enters additively through a set of age dummies common to both groups.

estimator.value: OLS difference-in-differences on a pre-trend-residualized outcome (equation 12), converted to an elasticity by equation (13)

estimation.specification: Equation (12); column 2: common age fixed effects; elasticity with respect to the net-of-tax rate by equation (13)
fixed_effects: age (full set of age dummies, common across treatment and control groups)
controls: group-specific linear pre-trend (outcome residualized, estimated on 1983-1986)

heterogeneity.dimension: control group (below-top bracket versus bottom bracket)
heterogeneity.finding: Panel A compares the top bracket to everyone below it; panel B compares the top bracket to the bottom bracket only. key_assumptions.supported_by: Observed pre-reform trends in Figures 3-6; all table estimates are additionally adjusted for group-specific linear pre-trends estimated on 1983-1986.

claims.statement: A higher net-of-tax interest rate 1 − τ on negative capital income reduced log(interest expenses) among Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 assigned to the top tax bracket in every year 1984-1986 (column 1: no age controls).

treatment.label: Net-of-tax rate 1 − τ on negative capital income

register_source.value: Danish Ministry of Taxation, statutory marginal tax rates on capital income (Figure 1)

definition.value: The elasticity is ε = α̂_3 / [Δlog(1 − τ^T) − Δlog(1 − τ^C)] (equation 13), where Δlog(1 − τ^g) is the reform-induced change in the net-of-tax rate on negative capital income for group g between 1986 and 1987. The reform raised this rate by 81 percent for the top group, 29 percent for the middle group and −6 percent for the bottom group.

timing.value: Change in the statutory net-of-tax rate between 1986 and 1987.

register_source.value: IND (Indkomst, Income) individual income tax records; interest expenses are third-party reported by lenders

definition.value: Natural log of total deductible interest expenses of homeowners, which include interests paid on mortgage debt, consumer debt and other types of loans; mortgage interest cannot be observed separately over the analysis period. The outcome entering equation (12) is residualized on a group-specific linear pre-trend estimated on 1983-1986.

timing.value: Measured annually; the coefficient is the average effect over the ten post-reform years (1987-1996) relative to the pre-reform years.

units.value: elasticity of interest expenses with respect to the net-of-tax rate 1 − τ (unitless)

magnitude.interpretation: we estimate an elasticity of interest expenses with respect to the net-of-tax rate between 0.12 and 0.25 in absolute value across control groups

estimand.target_population: High-income (top-bracket) Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 treated by the 1987 reform, relative to taxpayers below the top bracket (middle and bottom brackets combined) in every year 1984-1986
estimand.time_horizon: average effect over the ten post-reform years 1987-1996

population.description: Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 assigned to the top tax bracket in every year 1984-1986 (treatments) versus taxpayers below the top bracket in every year 1984-1986 (controls)
population.selection: Sample selection: individuals must be observed in every year of the panel (1983-1996), be aged 20-80, and be in the same tax bracket in all three pre-reform years 1984-1986 (bracket switchers, about 13 percent of the sample, are dropped); individuals whose owner/renter status cannot be assigned are dropped. The outcome is only defined for homeowners, so the sample is effectively conditioned on homeownership.

identification.source_of_variation: The 1987 Danish tax reform, which introduced dual income taxation and taxed negative capital income at the bottom rate. It raised the net-of-tax interest rate on negative capital income by 81 percent for the top bracket, 29 percent for the middle bracket, and lowered it by 6 percent for the bottom bracket.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the 1987 reform, the outcome of the top-bracket group and of taxpayers below the top bracket (middle and bottom brackets combined) in every year 1984-1986 would have evolved in parallel (after absorbing life-cycle/age effects and a group-specific linear pre-trend).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Observed pre-reform trends in Figures 3-6; all table estimates are additionally adjusted for group-specific linear pre-trends estimated on 1983-1986.

formal.statement: E[Y(0)_top,post − Y(0)_top,pre] = E[Y(0)_control,post − Y(0)_control,pre]

key_assumptions.assumption: Homogeneous responsiveness: the below-top control group is itself partly treated (the middle bracket saw a 29 percent rise in the net-of-tax rate), so the difference-in-differences recovers the elasticity only if treatments and controls respond homogeneously to the tax price.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the trade-off explicitly and reports the top-versus-bottom comparison (panel B), which does not require it.

formal.statement: The tax-price elasticity is constant across the top and below-top groups.

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference between treatment and control groups: the estimate is a partial-equilibrium (micro) elasticity that takes the rental rate r and the mortgage interest rate m as given, so the reform's general-equilibrium effect on prices is assumed not to shift the control group's outcome.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper flags the micro-versus-macro distinction, and Section V separately estimates a national house-price effect.

implies_edges.from: equilibrium house and rental prices

formal.statement: No edge from the treated group's reform exposure to the control group's outcome (no spillover through equilibrium house and rental prices).

homeownership in the given year

formal.statement: The analysis conditions on panel survival, bracket stability 1984-1986, and on homeownership.

implies_edges.from: Net-of-tax rate 1 − τ on negative capital income

formal.statement: No edge from the (future) 1987 reform to pre-1987 outcomes.

key_assumptions.assumption: Age effects are modelled as stated by column 1: no age controls: the DiD is only free of differential life-cycle composition if the age specification used in this column absorbs it.

formal.statement: Age enters additively through no age term.

estimator.value: OLS difference-in-differences on a pre-trend-residualized outcome (equation 12), converted to an elasticity by equation (13)

anchor_quote.text: The analysis is based on a difference-in-differences (DiD) design exploiting the 1987 tax reform.

claims.statement: A higher net-of-tax interest rate 1 − τ on negative capital income reduced log(interest expenses) among Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 assigned to the top tax bracket in every year 1984-1986 (column 1: no age controls).

treatment.label: Net-of-tax rate 1 − τ on negative capital income

register_source.value: Danish Ministry of Taxation, statutory marginal tax rates on capital income (Figure 1)

definition.value: The elasticity is ε = α̂_3 / [Δlog(1 − τ^T) − Δlog(1 − τ^C)] (equation 13), where Δlog(1 − τ^g) is the reform-induced change in the net-of-tax rate on negative capital income for group g between 1986 and 1987. The reform raised this rate by 81 percent for the top group, 29 percent for the middle group and −6 percent for the bottom group.

timing.value: Change in the statutory net-of-tax rate between 1986 and 1987.

register_source.value: IND (Indkomst, Income) individual income tax records; interest expenses are third-party reported by lenders

definition.value: Natural log of total deductible interest expenses of homeowners, which include interests paid on mortgage debt, consumer debt and other types of loans; mortgage interest cannot be observed separately over the analysis period. The outcome entering equation (12) is residualized on a group-specific linear pre-trend estimated on 1983-1986.

timing.value: Measured annually; the coefficient is the average effect over the ten post-reform years (1987-1996) relative to the pre-reform years.

units.value: elasticity of interest expenses with respect to the net-of-tax rate 1 − τ (unitless)

magnitude.interpretation: we estimate an elasticity of interest expenses with respect to the net-of-tax rate between 0.12 and 0.25 in absolute value across control groups

estimand.target_population: High-income (top-bracket) Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 treated by the 1987 reform, relative to taxpayers in the bottom bracket in every year 1984-1986, who are (almost) entirely untreated
estimand.time_horizon: average effect over the ten post-reform years 1987-1996

population.description: Danish taxpayers aged 20-80 assigned to the top tax bracket in every year 1984-1986 (treatments) versus taxpayers in the bottom bracket in every year 1984-1986 (controls)
population.selection: Sample selection: individuals must be observed in every year of the panel (1983-1996), be aged 20-80, and be in the same tax bracket in all three pre-reform years 1984-1986 (bracket switchers, about 13 percent of the sample, are dropped); individuals whose owner/renter status cannot be assigned are dropped. The outcome is only defined for homeowners, so the sample is effectively conditioned on homeownership.

identification.source_of_variation: The 1987 Danish tax reform, which introduced dual income taxation and taxed negative capital income at the bottom rate. It raised the net-of-tax interest rate on negative capital income by 81 percent for the top bracket, 29 percent for the middle bracket, and lowered it by 6 percent for the bottom bracket.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the 1987 reform, the outcome of the top-bracket group and of taxpayers in the bottom bracket in every year 1984-1986, who are (almost) entirely untreated would have evolved in parallel (after absorbing life-cycle/age effects and a group-specific linear pre-trend).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Observed pre-reform trends in Figures 3-6; all table estimates are additionally adjusted for group-specific linear pre-trends estimated on 1983-1986.

formal.statement: E[Y(0)_top,post − Y(0)_top,pre] = E[Y(0)_control,post − Y(0)_control,pre]

key_assumptions.assumption: The bottom-bracket control group is (almost) entirely untreated, so no homogeneity-of-response assumption is needed; the cost is that parallel trends is more tenuous between the top and bottom brackets.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The reform reduced the net-of-tax rate by only 6 percent for the bottom group; the paper states that this comparison does not require the homogeneity assumption.

formal.statement: Y(0) = Y(1) for the bottom-bracket control group.

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference between treatment and control groups: the estimate is a partial-equilibrium (micro) elasticity that takes the rental rate r and the mortgage interest rate m as given, so the reform's general-equilibrium effect on prices is assumed not to shift the control group's outcome.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper flags the micro-versus-macro distinction, and Section V separately estimates a national house-price effect.

implies_edges.from: equilibrium house and rental prices

formal.statement: No edge from the treated group's reform exposure to the control group's outcome (no spillover through equilibrium house and rental prices).

key_assumptions.assumption: Sample selection: individuals must be observed in every year of the panel (1983-1996), be aged 20-80, and be in the same tax bracket in all three pre-reform years 1984-1986 (bracket switchers, about 13 percent of the sample, are dropped); individuals whose owner/renter status cannot be assigned are dropped. The outcome is only defined for homeowners, so the sample is effectively conditioned on homeownership. These conditioning events are assumed not to be differentially affected by the reform.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the panel and bracket-stability restrictions and the share of the sample they drop.

homeownership in the given year

formal.statement: The analysis conditions on panel survival, bracket stability 1984-1986, and on homeownership.

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: outcomes in the pre-reform years 1984-1986, which are used to assign treatment status and to estimate the group-specific linear pre-trend, are not already responding to the 1987 reform.

implies_edges.from: Net-of-tax rate 1 − τ on negative capital income

formal.statement: No edge from the (future) 1987 reform to pre-1987 outcomes.

key_assumptions.assumption: Age effects are modelled as stated by column 1: no age controls: the DiD is only free of differential life-cycle composition if the age specification used in this column absorbs it.

formal.statement: Age enters additively through no age term.

controls: group-specific linear pre-trend (outcome residualized, estimated on 1983-1986)
